The digest runs through two trigger paths. In [src/instrumentation.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5619380e-4cb9-462b-a34d-2dc3676a5ff6/src/instrumentation.ts), `register()` starts the in-process scheduler on the Node.js runtime. In [scheduler.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5619380e-4cb9-462b-a34d-2dc3676a5ff6/src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts), `tick()` runs every minute and enqueues `digest-email` at a 60-minute cadence; `drain()` and `runHandler()` in [queue.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5619380e-4cb9-462b-a34d-2dc3676a5ff6/src/server/jobs/queue.ts) dispatch it to `runDigestEmailJob(new Date())`. Separately, `POST` in [the cron route](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5619380e-4cb9-462b-a34d-2dc3676a5ff6/src/app/api/cron/digest/route.ts) checks the `x-taskflow-cron` secret and calls the job directly. [event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5619380e-4cb9-462b-a34d-2dc3676a5ff6/src/server/services/event-registry.ts) also bridges a `digest.due` event into the queue; the queue handler runs the same whole-job scan, rather than using the event’s recipient and window payload.

`runDigestEmailJob()` in [digest-email-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5619380e-4cb9-462b-a34d-2dc3676a5ff6/src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts) first calls `listOrgIdsForRollup(50)` in [usage-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5619380e-4cb9-462b-a34d-2dc3676a5ff6/src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts). That selects at most 50 IDs from **organization usage rows**, ordered by oldest measurement; it does not scan or paginate through every organization. For each ID, the job loads the organization. `shouldRunForOrg()` requires it to be unarchived and the current UTC hour to equal `settings.digestHourUtc`. The job also checks `digest_email` using `isEnabled()` with the organization’s flag context.

For each eligible organization, `listDigestRecipients()` in [digest-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5619380e-4cb9-462b-a34d-2dc3676a5ff6/src/server/services/digest-service.ts) delegates to `listDigestSubscribers()` in [notification-preference-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5619380e-4cb9-462b-a34d-2dc3676a5ff6/src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts). That query returns distinct users with at least one preference row in the organization whose `digestOnly` is true; it does not require every kind to be marked digest-only.

The source material is notification rows created earlier. In [notification-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5619380e-4cb9-462b-a34d-2dc3676a5ff6/src/server/services/notification-service.ts), `registerFanOut()` subscribes to events such as assignments, overdue issues, comments, mentions, and member joins. Its handlers call `notify()`, which excludes the actor, resolves each recipient’s channels from their preference, skips recipients with no channels, and inserts notification rows. Those rows begin unread. A digest subscriber can therefore have no row for an event, for example when they caused it themselves or muted all channels for that kind.

For each subscriber, the job sets the window to the **24 hours ending at the job’s supplied `now`**, then calls `buildDigest()`. That function reloads the organization and rechecks the feature flag, then calls `listUnreadSince()` in [notification-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5619380e-4cb9-462b-a34d-2dc3676a5ff6/src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts). The query selects that person’s unread rows in the organization created at or after the window start, newest first. `buildDigest()` filters out rows after the window end, maps the remainder to `DigestEntry` values containing notification ID, kind, title, link, and occurrence time, and keeps at most 50. It does **not** filter those rows by whether their individual kinds are marked digest-only.

If there is at least one entry and the user still exists, `renderDigest()` passes the recipient name, entry count, window, and first title to `renderEmail()` in [email-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5619380e-4cb9-462b-a34d-2dc3676a5ff6/src/server/services/email-service.ts). The current renderer produces a generic table of those properties; it does not pass the entry list to the separate `DigestEmail` component. `sendEmail()` currently logs the message metadata rather than delivering through an outbound mail transport. After it returns, the job marks each included notification read, which normally prevents those same entries from appearing in a later run.

A subscribed person consequently gets no digest when their organization is absent from that limited usage-row batch, is missing or archived, is outside its configured UTC hour, or lacks the enabled feature; when the user record is missing; or when no eligible unread notification remains in the window. Reading notifications before the job runs, a quiet day, or events that never produced a row can all leave the bundle empty. Errors during a recipient’s build, render, send, or marking are caught and logged as a failed recipient. The read marking suppresses repeats of included entries, but it is not a strict once-per-day delivery record: new unread rows or entries left beyond the 50-entry cap can be picked up by another run in the same hour.
